title: MT82 Manual Transmission: Construction and Identification
introduction:
This overview covers the MT82 manual transmission. I use the internal drawing to understand the shaft layout, then the identification label to establish which unit I am looking at.

Synchronizers act like speed matchmakers: they bring rotating parts toward compatible speeds before engagement. That makes the different synchronizer arrangements worth understanding, but it does not turn a reluctant shift into an instant diagnosis. This page explains construction and identification; internal repair, bearing installation and fluid service need their matching procedures.

edits.why: The name, shaft drawing and construction details describe the same gearbox from different angles.

edits.text: The MT82 is a fully synchronized 6-speed manual transmission with reverse gear. The MT82 name incorporates the distance between the main shaft and counter shaft, shown between their centerlines in the drawing:
edits.why: The drawing measures shaft spacing, rather than gear diameter or housing width.

edits.text: Read the MT82 designation as follows:
82 is the centerline distance between the main shaft and counter shaft, in millimeters.
edits.why: The dimension lines in the drawing originate at the shaft centers.

edits.text: The transmission has a coaxial three-shaft layout: the input and output shafts lie on a single axis. All gear wheels have helical teeth and remain constantly engaged with their mating gears. Maximum design torque is 480 Nm. The selector rods pass through a center bearing mounting plate bolted to the housing, and that plate also supports the main selector shaft. All gear selector forks and shift forks are forged steel. The transmission bearing arrangement requires neither preload nor shims. To accommodate shaft expansion as temperature rises, one bearing can slide in its seat while the other is pressed fully home. For gear selection, 1st and 2nd gear use triple synchronizers, 3rd and 4th gear use double synchronizers, and only 5th, 6th and reverse gear use single synchronizers. The transmission fluid is designed for the transmission’s entire service life and does not require changing during servicing.
edits.why: The input shaft receives engine rotation, and the output carries the selected drive toward the driveline. Constant mesh describes the mating gear teeth; synchronization prepares the rotating parts for selection. The sliding bearing accommodates heat expansion without making every bearing a loose fit. These are construction principles, not bearing-fitting instructions, and the torque figure is a design rating rather than a tightening specification.
Use the illustration’s callouts with the table to separate the replacement part number from manufacturing and build information. The example label is not a universal ordering code.

edits.text: Find the transmission identification tag on the RH side of the transmission near the driveshaft flange.
edits.why: RH means right-hand; the driveshaft flange identifies the output end. The enlarged label shows which fields the table describes, but this overview gives neither physical access steps nor a convention for decoding the build fields.
